chunks: And ʿAlī al-Ṣāʾigh asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said:
I take on work, then assign it to the young workers, who work with me for two-thirds. He عليه السلام said: “That is not proper unless you work along with them.”
I said: “Then I melt it for them.” He عليه السلام said: “That is work, so there is no harm in it.”

key_terms.أَتَقَبَّلُ: I accept or take on contracted work
key_terms.أُذِيبُهُ: I melt it, meaning I perform part of the craft process
key_terms.الْعَمَلَ: the work or job being contracted
key_terms.الْغِلْمَانِ: young workers or lads employed in the task
key_terms.بِالثُّلُثَيْنِ: for two-thirds of the proceeds or compensation
key_terms.تُعَالِجَ: to work personally with them or directly engage in the labor
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm, meaning it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to subcontract work to laborers for a share of the payment without personally working on it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on taking contracted work and passing it to laborers for a share of the earnings. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام permits it only when the contractor also contributes actual labor, and clarifies that melting the material counts as such work.
